title: PISTON, LINEAR ACTUATING CYLINDER / NSN 1650-01-206-1949 / CH-53 HELICOPTER

title: QELS Dynamic Light Scattering Detector
description: OPQR has a requirement to obtain an advanced dynamic light scattering detector to enhance characterization capabilities for emerging pharmaceutical products and complex biologics. For a quoter's detector to be deemed acceptable, the following salient characteristics shall be met: QELS Dynamic Light Scattering Detector: Real-time hydrodynamic radius measurement capability that operates inline with Field-Flow Fractionation separation to provide simultaneous size characterization as samples elute from the FFF system. Compatibility with Existing FFF System: Must be fully compatible with and integrate seamlessly into the existing FFF system, including hardware connections, software integration with chromatography software, and synchronized data acquisition with existing MALS detectors. High-Sensitivity Detection: Capable of measuring hydrodynamic radii across a wide dynamic range from approximately 10 nm to 1000 nm to accommodate diverse sample types including proteins, protein aggregates, liposomes, and lipid nanoparticles. Orthogonal Size Validation: Provides diffusion-based size measurements that complement separation-based FFF analysis, enabling validation of particle size distributions and detection of sub-populations or aggregates that may not be fully resolved by separation alone. Data Correlation and Analysis: Integrated software functionality that enables direct correlation between molecular weight data from MALS detection and hydrodynamic size from DLS detection to provide comprehensive analysis of absolute molar mass, root-mean-square radius, and hydrodynamic radius. Data Output: Generates validated, audit-trail-compliant data files suitable for regulatory submissions and scientific publications, with full integration into existing software platform for unified data processing and reporting. Maintenance and Support: Technical support, software updates, preventive maintenance, and alignment with FDA's quality assurance requirements for analytical instrumentation. 3.4 Deliverables Ref Description Quantities Required Due Date 3 Quasi-Elastic Light Scattering Unit for FFF 1 120 days after award 3 Installation, instrument qualification and training 1 120 days after contract award. Detector hardware with all necessary cables, connectors, and mounting hardware for integration with existing FFF system. Software licensing and installation files compatible with current chromatography software version. User manuals, technical specifications, and standard operating procedure templates provided in digital format via download or physical media (CD/DVD). CD, DVD and hard copies of deliverables shall not be required to be returned to the Contractor. Deliverables are delivered to the following address: U.S Food and Drug Administration Center for Drug Evaluation and Research / Office of Pharmaceutical Quality / Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research Attn: TBD 645 S Newstead Avenue St. Louis, M0 63110 3Schedule: Delivery shall be no later than 120 days after contract award. Vendor is responsible for coordination with FDA staff for installation and integration with existing FFF system. FDA staff will provide access to laboratory space and existing instrumentation for installation activities. 3.6 Maintenance and Technical Support: At minimum the contractor must: Provide support via email, phone, and/or web conference for troubleshooting and technical assistance. Provide on-site installation, integration testing, and performance qualification of the detector with existing FFF-MALS system. Provide on-site training for FDA staff on detector operation, data analysis, method development, and routine maintenance procedures. Inspection and Acceptance Criteria Partial acceptance is made upon delivery of all the parts. Full acceptance is made after completion of Installation and Operational Qualification (IQ/OQ) by the contractor that the system meets all the specifications and requirements. Terms of Use Fixed Term License: FDA shall the ability to purchase a new subscription after the original subscription expires to continue the use of the software and to gain access to technical support and product upgrades. Period of Performance The period of performance is 12 months from the installation date of the system. The delivery of the entire system with accessories as outlined in the SOW should be completed within 120 days of award. Instrument installation and qualification should be completed within 120 days of award. Instrument familiarization and training should be completed on the day of installation. title: Endoscopy Systems
description: Under FDA guidance, this OSEL-DIDSR collaboration requires an endoscope to maximize scientific research capacity throughout the center and agency. An endoscope allows OSEL researchers to develop bench testing methods for evaluating the safety and effectiveness of endoscopy devices. The Government requires an endoscope system (Endoscope) with the following minimum requirements: The Endoscope shall be shipped to the following address: Attention to: TBD 10903 New Hampshire Ave WO62-3133, US FDA Silver Spring, MD 20993- Shipping cost is included in the total purchase price. The Endoscope shall include the video processor, colonoscope, medical display, and cart that are interoperable with each other. Once assembled, these components shall operate as a fully functional endoscopy system that can acquire and display live image. The video processor shall satisfy the following requirements: The video processor shall be an FDA-cleared 510(k) medical device. The database is publicly available at 510(k) Premarket Notification. The light source shall be integrated within the video processor. The light source shall use three (3) or more LEDs to synthesize different spectra. The video processor shall have the white light mode. The video processor shall have two (2) or more narrow-band imaging (NBI) modes that utilize different optical spectra generated by the LED-based light source. The NBI modes shall be FDA-cleared for visualizing biological features such as blood vessels or mucosal surfaces. The video processor shall have two (2) or more digital color enhancement modes that utilize different digital image processing techniques. These color enhancement modes shall be FDA-cleared under the FDA product code �PEA�. The video processor shall have the following video output ports and video formats: 12G-SDI (3840x2160x60p) 3G-SDI (1920x1080x60p) HD-SDI (1900x1080x60i) The video processor shall have the capability of saving still images in a standard image file format such as TIFF or JPEG. The video processor shall have the capability of saving video clips in a standard video file format. The colonoscope shall satisfy the following requirements: The colonoscope shall be an FDA-cleared 510(k) colonoscope device. The direction of view shall be forward viewing. The field of view shall be 170 � or wider. The depth of field shall cover the range of 5-100 mm or wider. The angulation (up/down/right/left) shall be 180�/180�/160�/160� or larger. The colonoscope shall have a water nozzle. The insertion tube diameter shall be 12.8 mm or smaller. The colonoscope shall have an instrument channel with diameter of 3.7 mm or larger. The medical display shall satisfy the following requirements: The signal input ports shall include: 12G-SDI 3G-SDI Display Port HDMI DVI The pixel count shall be equal to or greater than 3840x2160 pixels (4K). The display size (diagonal) shall be equal to or greater than 32 inches. All components in the system shall be powered by the standard 120 volts, 60 Hertz alternating current power in the U.S. The Endoscope shall include a total system warranty for at least one (1) year, inclusive of any parts, labor, travel, and shipping cost to return the system to the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) standards.The Contractor shall deliver the endoscope within six (6) weeks of contract award. The Contractor shall provide a one (1)-year warranty period following system acceptance.

description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Solicitation Number: W9127N26QA137 Project Title: XJ2 Breaker Overhaul, Location: John Day Lock and Dam, NAICS Code: 811310- Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance Product Service Code (PSC): J061 - MAINT/REPAIR/REBUILD OF EQUIPMENT- ELECTRIC WIRE AND POWER DISTRIBUTION EQUIPMENT 1.0 Special Notice Details The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Portland District (NWP) - John Day Lock and Dam intends to solicit and award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) commercial supply contract to provide full-service maintenance, emergency response, preventive maintenance, baseline inspection, and operating mechanism overhaul/adaptation for or the ABB/Hitachi Energy Type HECI-5R Generator Circuit Breaker (Serial No. HA 2145-10). For the Technical Scope Refinement: Following final technical coordination between the requiring activity (USACE Engineering) and the OEM representative, the Performance Work Statement (PWS REV2) was administratively updated to reflect the detailed breakdown of tasks: 1. Emergency Response Time: The emergency on-site arrival window was extended from 3 hours to 96 hours to align with regional technician travel logistics from OEM facilities in the Pacific Northwest. 2. Specific Sub-Tasks: The PWS explicitly itemizes: a. on-site installation and adaptation of the Government-Furnished HMB-4.5 mechanism; b. off-site factory overhaul of the removed legacy HMB-4 mechanism at the OEM facility; c. on-site technical training for USACE powerhouse personnel; and d. routine monthly maintenance. Nexus Power Solution LLC 2139 S WEST TEMPLE, SOUTH SALT LAKE, UTAH 84115 A competitive solicitation package will not be posted to SAM.gov. 2.0 Technical & Market Research Justification Market research was conducted by contacting Hitachi Energy USA Inc. regarding field engineering services, maintenance support, and GFE adaptation for the John Day Dam breaker. Hitachi Energy confirmed that direct service orders and regional technician dispatches for Oregon are exclusively handled by their authorized sales and service representative. Hitachi Energy (formerly ABB) is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and holds all proprietary engineering drawings, manufacturing specifications, tolerances, and calibration data for the HECI-5R breaker and the HMB series hydromechanical spring operating mechanisms. title: MEARNG F550 Emergency Light Installation
description: The Maine Army National Guard (MEARNG) requires the professional installation of a complete, government-furnished, emergency response vehicle police-style flashing light system and a battery charging system onto a Government-owned Ford F-550 Vehicle Mounted Radiation Detection System (VMRDS). The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, tools, materials (excluding specified government-furnished equipment), and expertise to complete the installation. Scope of Work: The contractor is required to perform the following installations and integrations on the Ford F-550 vehicle: Equipment Installation: Install all Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE) at specified locations. This includes a Whelen Inner Edge light assembly, a Whelen Core and Controller unit, and various Whelen body, slim, and trio lights. System Integration: Professionally integrate all lighting components with the central controller. All wiring must be routed, secured, protected with grommets where necessary, and concealed appropriately. Power System Installation: Install one Kussmaul battery tender complete with an auto-eject shore power connection to charge the vehicle's batteries. Functional Testing: Conduct a full functional test of the integrated lighting system and the power system in the presence of a Government representative to demonstrate proper functionality. Vehicle Restoration: Upon completion, repair any damage to the vehicle resulting from installation activities and ensure all work areas are cleaned of debris, materials, and tools. Government Furnished Equipment (GFE): The Government will provide the following major components for installation: One (1) Whelen Inner Edge light assembly One (1) Whelen Core and Controller unit Two (2) Whelen slim lights (for front grill) Eight (8) Whelen body lights Two (2) Whelen trio lights Two (2) Whelen slim lights (for front fenders) One (1) Kussmaul battery tender Contractor Requirements: Provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials (except GFE), and supervision. Ensure all employees possess the required skillsets or licensing to install the lighting system according to manufacturer specifications. The place of performance will be the contractor's installation facility. The period of performance for the installation shall not exceed one week. Period of Performance: The work must be completed within one (1) week from the start date. Questions: May be submitted to the points of contact below. The due date for questions is 09SEP2026. Submission Instructions: All quotes must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist, Thomas J. Ryan, at thomas.j.ryan36.civ@army.mil and the Contracting Officer, Darlene Howes, at darlene.r.howes.civ@army.mil. Quotes must include a completed SF 1449 and a separate Technical Proposal responding to the evaluation criteria outlined in the FAR 52.212-1 and 52.212-2 Addenda.

SOLE SOURCE AUTHORITY AND JUSTIFICATION The proposed contract action is for commercial products for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO Part 12 (Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Commercial Products below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold). The proprietary Compunetix hardware and TDI-13II touchscreen consoles are technically necessary to integrate natively with the existing Range Communication System (RASS) voice distribution switching architecture at Edwards AFB. These specific hardware models are currently certified, accredited, and baseline-integrated under the existing RASS Authority to Operate (ATO). The introduction of non-certified or non-interoperable hardware would invalidate the RASS ATO, introduce unacceptable mission risk, and cause severe schedule delays to active flight test programs. Compunetix, Inc. (CAGE: 8C319) is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of this proprietary hardware and does not utilize third-party authorized distributors or resellers for this specialized product line. 3. INSTRUCTIONS TO INTERESTED PARTIES This notice of intent is not a competitive request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Capability statements must demonstrate the vendor�s ability to provide identical, form-fit-and-function, OEM-certified Compunetix components that natively interface with the existing VCSU switching matrix and maintain compliance with the RASS ATO security baseline without modification. Responses must be submitted electronically via email to Contract Specialist Christina M. Day at christina.day.6@us.af.mil. title: Purchase and install of wall-attached telescopic bleacher system and removal of existing bleachers
description: ***UPDATE*** Please see attached questions and answers document in attachments. This solicitation is now due on 16 Sept at 1400 (2 PM CST) to the below POCs (Mrs. Lauren Rodgers and MSgt Wenas) Amendment to solictation FA813626Q0011: This solicitation is hereby amended to revise the product description from brand-name-only requirement to brand-name-or-equal requirement. 1. Products other than the specified brand name may be offered provided the proposed product meets or exceeds all stated salient physical. functional, and performance charachteristics outlined in the updated Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors proposing an equal product must identify the manufacturer of proposed product and shall provide suffient descriptive literature, specifications and other technical information neccessary for the Governmenrt to determine whether the proposed product meets the stated requirements. 2. The previously posted Statement of Need (SON) has been replaced by the Statement of Work (SOW). The SOW is amended to revise the Government's requirements from brand-name to brand-name or equal. The revision permits products manufactured by sources other than the originally specified manufacturer, provided the proposed product satisfies the Government's stated minimum requirements. 3. The previously applicable Brand Name Justification, supporting the brand-name-only requirement identified in the original solicitation is no longer applicable due to the revision of the governements requirement, and that document has therefore been removed from this solicitation. ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ The response deadline for this solicitation is 14 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. A site visit will be offered (optional) on 1 September 2026 so vendors can ensure accurate measurements. Questions are due 3 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. All interested parties should contact Lauren Rodgers, lauren.rodgers.5@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer MSgt Kristoforus Wenas, kristoforus.wenas.1@us.af.mil to schedule site visit. This RFQ is being issued on SAM.gov as a small business set aside. Purchase is required to satisfy Youth Center seating- � The current bleachers were installed 25 years ago and have reached the end of their service life. Replacement is necessary to ensure continued safety, reliability for all Youth Center spectators. The vendor will provide MAXAM telescopic bleachers manufactured by Hussey Seating Company, or equivelant, that will perform full installation of the system. The scope of work includes demolition and removal of the existing bleacher system. The new bleachers will be attached to the wall and designed to retract to extend maximum available floor space. System Classification � Brand & Model: Hussey Seating Company MAXAM Telescopic Series (or approved equivalent meeting identical dimensional and safety tolerances). � Design: Wall-attached, manually operated, multi-tier retractable spectator seating system designed specifically for indoor gymnasium environments. Physical Dimensions � Installed Length: Approximately 45 feet (45' total continuous length). � Fully Deployed Depth: Maximum 9 feet, 1 inch (9' 1") from the mounting wall. � Row Quantity & Spacing: 5 rows (tiers) of seating with a standard 22-inch to 24-inch row spacing to ensure adequate legroom and egress. Material & Construction � Understructure Frame: Heavy-duty, high-tensile structural steel shapes forming a rigid, self-supporting understructure, finished with a corrosion-resistant black powder coat. � Decks & Under-decking: Minimum 5/8-inch exterior-grade plywood panels with a durable, non-slip textured poly-wear surface overlay. � Seating Type: CourtSide collection (or equivelant) contoured HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene) seats, 10-inch (254 mm) depth, featuring an anatomical curved design with a front "waterfall" edge to alleviate thigh pressure. Demolition & Site Prep � Complete demolition and removal of existing 25-year-old bleachers with zero damage to surrounding walls, gym floor, or utility lines. � 100% damage-free. Any accidental damage must be repaired/restored to original condition at contractor expense within 5 business days. � 100% Inspection by COR and Youth Center Facility Manager. Operational Method � Operation: Manual operation utilizing a high-efficiency pull-handle/draw-bar system. � Tracking: Must feature self-supporting first-row wheels and structural guide tracks to allow smooth, single-operator extension and retraction without binding. � Operational Training: Provide comprehensive, on-site operational and safety training to at least five (5) designated Youth Center staff members. Accessibility Compliance (ADA) � Wheelchair Spaces: Minimum of four (4) integrated, ADA-compliant wheelchair seating locations recovered within the footprint. � Companion Seating: Adjacent companion seating structurally integrated as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the International Building Code (IBC). Safety & Egress Features � Aisle Handrails: Center-aisle, self-storing, or removable structural steel handrails with round profiles, finished in high-visibility safety colors. � End Rails (Guardrails): Full-height steel guardrails at both open ends of the bleacher system, meeting a minimum lateral load requirement of 50 lbs/ft at the top rail. � Locking Mechanisms: Automatic mechanical tier locks that securely lock each row in the fully extended position to prevent accidental retraction during occupancy. Structural Load Standards � Compliance: Must conform to IBC (International Building Code) and ICC 300 (Standard for Bleachers, Folding and Telescopic Seating, and Grandstands) load ratings. � Active Live Load: Minimum 120 lbs/sq ft active horizontal framework capacity. � Sway Load: 24 lbs/linear ft parallel to seats; 10 lbs/linear ft perpendicular to seats. Execution & Safety Certification � Installation: Must be executed by a factory-certified installer. � Testing: Installer must conduct a formal structural and operational safety test prior to government acceptance. ***Additional requirements listed in attached SOW. Delivery/Services Required: The contractor shall be responsible for all freight and shipping costs to provide FOB Destination inside delivery to Tinker AFB, Oklahoma 73145. Delivery is required 60 days After Receipt of Order (ARO). Eligibility: The applicable NAICS Code for this requirement is 337127. The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this effort is 7195. This NAICS is the only applicable NAICS for this effort. To be considered for this award, contractor must have this NAICS on their profile. If it is not on contractor profile, request it to be added. title: NSN 4810-01-187-9275, PART NUMBER 300310-101, DESCRIPTION: SLEEVE AND SLIDE, DI
description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Richmond is issuing this sources sought as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for a SLEEVE AND SLIDE, DI. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 332911. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. If your organization has the potential capacity to provide the above listed supplies, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, emails address, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) Provide supplies consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) provide supplies under a firm-fixed price acquisition contract. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by 4:30 PM, EST., September 16, 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to Courtney.Minor@dla.mil If you have any questions concerning this opportunity please contact: Courtney Minor at (804) 914-9258. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. Potential sources shall be capable of furnishing all labor, materials, facilities and equipment required to accomplish the new manufacture of the item(s). Generally, this entails the procurement/manufacture of component parts, inspection, testing, preservation/packaging, and shipping. Additionally, potential sources may be responsible for supply chain management, logistics planning, forecasting production requirements, long-lead time parts procurement, diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortage issues, and shipping serviceable assets. The unit prices will be established at the time of a contract award. The specific requirement for this effort is below: Part Number: 300310-101 Nomenclature: SLEEVE AND SLIDE, DI NSN: 4810-01-187-9275 Estimated Requirement: 42 each Technical Orders and Qualification Requirements are not available.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Facilities and Equipment Maintenance (FEM) System Analyst Support
description: This is a Special Notice prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) subpart 5.2, Synopsis of Proposed Contract Actions. A Solicitation will not be posted, however any firm who believes it can perform the required services may give written notice to the Contracting Officer within 15 days of publication of this Special Notice. Supporting evidence must be in sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to comply with the requirement. Responses received will be evaluated; however a determination by the Government to compete the requirement based on the responses to this Special Notice is solely the discretion of the Government. The US Army Corps of Engineers Mission Support Battalion (UMSB) intends to award a sole source fixed-price contract to Battelle Memorial Institute for service to optimize expand, and analyze the FEM system. This Notice of Intent to award a sole source contract is not a request for competitive proposals. Any responses or inquiries to this notice must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that competition will be advantageous to the Government. All information received from this notice shall be used for planning and market research purposes only. The determination to refrain from competing proposed contracts based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government will not pay for the preparation of any information submitted or use of such information. Acknowledgement of receipt of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified of the evaluation of the information received. Interested parties may express interest and provide a capability statement.

title: Rakennusurakointitöiden puitehankinta vuosille 2026 - 2029
description: Rakennusurakointitöiden puitehankinta vuosille 2026 - 2029 Naantalin kaupungin yksiköt (Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia rakennusurakointitöiden toteuttamisesta sopimuskaudelle. Hankinnan kohteena olevat työt toteutetaan joko erikseen minikilpailutettavina toimeksiantoina tai suoraan hankittavina töinä sopimusehtojen mukaisesti. Rakennusurakoita kilpailutetaan lisäksi kohdekohtaisilla urakkakilpailulla. Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.11.2026. Lisäksi Tilaaja varaa mahdollisuuden kahteen optiovuoteen (1+1). Optiolla tarkoitetaan mahdollisuutta sopimuksen jatkamiseen alkuperäisin ehdoin. Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä erikseen. Hankinta tullaan toteuttamaan puitejärjestelynä. Tilattavien töiden sisältö ja määrä eivät ole ennalta tiedossa eikä Tilaaja sitoudu mihinkään hankintamääriin sopimuskauden aikana. Pienurakat voivat sisältää rakennus-, maalaus-, matto-, tasoite-, vedeneristys- sekä laatoitus- ja teräsrakennetöitä. Urakat toteutetaan noudattaen rakennusalan yleisiä sopimusehtoja YSE 1998.,

title: Vaajakosken liikuntapuiston tulostaulu
description: Vaajakosken liikuntapuiston tulostaulu Jyväskylän kaupungin liikuntapalvelut pyytää tarjousta yhdestä (1) tulostaulusta/videotaulusta. Taulu sijoitetaan Vaajakosken liikuntapuistoon, joka on pääasiallisesti yleisurheilun, jalkapallon ja amerikkalaisen jalkapallon käytössä. Taulun toimitukseen tulee sisältyä tarvittavat ohjelmistot, ohjauslaitteet, asennus ja käytönopastus. Lisäksi hankintaan sisältyy taulun sähköistys tarjouspyynnössä olevan liitteen mukaisesti. Tulostaulun asennus suoritetaan tilaajan osoittamaan valmiiseen asennuspaikkaan. Asennuspaikan tekniset tiedot on esitetty tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Taulun teline on valmisteilla. Tulostaulun asennusvalmius on alustavan arvion mukaan viikosta 43 alkaen. Mikäli tulostaulun asennus tapahtuu peruskorjauksen ollessa käynnissä, tehdään valitun toimittajan kanssa alistamissopimus suhteessa taulun telineen päätoteuttajaan. Peruskorjauksen arvioitu keskeytyminen talvikauden ajaksi on 13.11. alkaen. Mikäli tulostaulun toimitus ja asennus tapahtuu tämän jälkeen, vastaa taulun toimittaja työmaan turvallisuudesta ja muista velvoitteista.,

STATEMENT OF WORK INTERIOR WAYFINDING SIGNAGE � VA MANCHESTER MEDICAL CENTER 718 Smyth Road, Manchester, NH 03104 Justification. The VA Medical Center, Manchester, NH (VAMCMNH) requires new standardized interior wayfinding signage to improve the ease with which Veterans and visitors navigate the campus. The intent is to update all directional signs to a uniform standard that improves visibility and clarity, and that coordinates with newly installed exterior signage. 3.1 Objectives VAMCMNH requires a turnkey wayfinding signage project. The Contractor shall design an overall wayfinding system, including departmental identification, directional, and ADA-compliant signage; fabricate; remove existing signage; and install new interior signage throughout the main building (approximately 290,000 SF, 7 stories, 3 major public entrances). The design shall standardize and unify signage using colors, symbols (Eagle, Mountain, and Seacoast motifs), cardinal points, and text, with field-replaceable inserts capable of in-house reprinting. The Contractor shall propose how the Medical Center's existing electronic directories at the three main entrances can be integrated into the overall wayfinding design. Design, fabrication, removal of existing signs, disposal, and installation of new signage includes, but is not limited to: department directories and sub-directories at elevators and major hallway intersections; ADA call-outs (wheelchair symbol, Braille compliance) at all applicable public spaces; and directional signage to restrooms, elevators, and waiting/check-out areas, wall- or ceiling-mounted as appropriate. The signage solution must be brand-name-or-equal to the Basis of Design signage system currently VA-approved, offering equal or greater function, fit, and finish, to maintain a consistent patient experience. 3.2 Design Requirements Signage shall align with VA's Technical Information Library (TIL) and National Standards, reflecting professional-quality workmanship. Signage shall leverage the facility's spatial organization and architectural features (destination zones, landmarks, shape, color). Signage shall be easy to recognize, consistent, clear, distinctive, and legible. Signage shall comply with current ADA/ABA Accessible Design Standards where required. The Contractor's signage shall be unified with existing exterior and retained interior signage. Insert templates shall be vendor-provided and compatible with VAMCMNH's internal reproduction resources where possible. All signage shall meet VA PG-18-10, Signage Design Manual guidelines, and all applicable Federal and VA safety/ADA requirements. 3.3 Services and Products The Contractor shall, at minimum: Perform a site review to verify locations, available areas, dimensions, wall types (drywall, concrete block, ceiling type, etc.), and potential conflicts. Provide monthly progress updates to the COR/VA Designer. Develop wayfinding/circulation solutions and sign location plans. Prepare conceptual designs (materials, finishes, color, typography, scale) for design-team review. Finalize all sign system design elements, fabrication specifications, graphics, and installation details. Prepare sign layouts based on final message schedules to determine sign/letter sizing. Provide final fabrication submittals based on approved design. Remove existing signage requiring removal; perform wall prep and repair (VA will supply paint). Fabricate and install new signage per the approved design. Develop an installation schedule ensuring timely, accurate, and code-compliant installation. Comply with VA PG-18-10 guidelines throughout. Estimated quantities: 50 Sub-directories/Directional signs 50 Stair signs 50 Overhead signs 32 Overhead bathroom signs 50 To Waiting Room/Check-out signs Compliance: Full ADA (tactile/Braille, 70% contrast, 5/8" minimum letter height, antimicrobial finishes, fire-rated as needed). 3.4 Quality and Workmanship Workmanship and materials shall meet all current VA standards. All shop drawings and material samples shall be submitted to the COR for approval before fabrication. Work shall comply with the International Building Code, NFPA 99 (Health Care Facilities Code), NFPA 13, and OSHA requirements. Where code and VA specifications conflict, the more stringent standard governs. All Contractor and subcontractor employees shall comply with the VA security management program, obtain and visibly wear a contractor badge at all times while on VA property, and clean all work areas daily (trash removed; VA dumpsters may not be used). 3.5 Project Meetings Contractor shall hold a kickoff meeting to review scheduling and milestones. Contractor shall hold regular review meetings with VA staff throughout programming, design, fabrication, and installation, with a minimum of four review meetings or until scope is completed. Contractor shall email the VA COR and CO a biweekly status report (progress, updated schedule, general status). 3.6 Contractor Training Requirements All Contractor/subcontractor employees shall hold, at minimum, a 10-hour OSHA-certified Construction Safety course and/or other relevant competency training. Training records shall be submitted to the COR for approval before installation begins. 3.7 Installation Schedule / Phasing Installation shall be scheduled Monday�Friday, 7:00 a.m.�4:30 p.m., unless evening/weekend hours are separately arranged with the VA Interior Designer/POC. title: CNF WATER SAMPLE TESTING
description: CNF WATER SAMPLE TESTING This solicitation is to establish a Firm-Fixed Price, Requirements, Non-Personal Services contract for water sample testing for the Forest Service, Chugach National Forest (CNF), Southcentral Alaska. Purpose: The purpose of this contract is to ensure compliance with federal and state drinking water regulations, obtain certified laboratory analyses, maintain operational readiness, and protect public health at forest service facilities. Description of Services: The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to perform water sample testing for the Forest Service, Chugach National Forest, located in Southcentral Alaska. Services shall include the testing and analysis of water samples for specified contaminants, including Coliform, Nitrate, Lead and Copper, Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs), Arsenic, and any additional testing required to ensure safe drinking water throughout Southcentral Alaska. Place of Performance: The work shall be performed at the contractor�s designated laboratory facility within 120 driving miles of both Girdwood and Moose Pass. Contract Type: The Government will award a Firm-Fixed Price, Requirements, Non-Personal Services contract with up to a 5-Year Ordering Period. Performance shall be made only as authorized by Task Orders issued IAW the Ordering Clause. Subject to any limitations in the Order Limitations Clause or elsewhere in this contract, the contractor shall furnish to the Government all services specified in the Schedule of Items and called for by orders issued IAW the Ordering Clause. description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Commercial Internet and Telecommunications Services (Spectrum) Notice ID: 140L1226Q0046 This is a Sole Source Notice posted in accordance with RFO 5.201(b)(1)(i). The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) intends to purchase, on a sole source basis, commercial internet access and related telecommunications services from Charter Communications Operating LLC (Spectrum) to support operations at specified BLM facilities in California. The requirement covers installation/activation of last mile facilities, handoff to Government premises equipment, static IP configuration as needed, and ongoing monthly service. This acquisition is necessary to maintain continuity of operations and ensure connectivity at these locations where Spectrum is the only responsible source with existing serviceable plant. This determination is based on program market research and site level technical reviews documenting the lack of alternative carriers with facilities in the immediate vicinity. This purchase will be conducted under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul commercial procedures at RFO 12.102. This action is justified under RFO 6.103-1(b), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. A firm fixed-price award is anticipated. The associated NAICS code for this requirement is 517111 (Wired Telecommunications Carriers). The vendor's SAM information is: Charter Communications Operating LLC (Spectrum), UEI MX16CA896HK5, CAGE 4WWK4 (Active registration; no exclusions). The applicable PSC is DG11 (IT and Telecom Network: Satellite Communications and Telecom Access Services). The attached sole source justification has been made available for review. No solicitation documents exist. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes or offers. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action lies solely within the discretion of the Government. Firms believing they have the capability to provide this requirement must submit written information showing clear and convincing evidence that they can deliver equivalent services to all listed BLM facilities using existing infrastructure without new construction or schedule risk, and that they can meet the Government's technical, performance, and continuity needs.

description: Combined Synopsis-Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services PURPOSE OF AMENDMENT 0004 The purpose of this amendment to RFQ 36C24126Q0547 is as follows: Extend the response due date for receipt of quotes to September 14 , 2026, at 5:00 PM Eastern Time. Change the method of procurement from a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside to a Total Small Business Set-Aside. This change is based on the Government's determination, following review of quotes received under the SDVOSB set-aside, that fair and reasonable pricing could not be obtained in accordance with FAR 19.1405(b)(2). This requirement remains within the small business industrial base, consistent with the SBA Nonmanufacturer Rule (NMR) waiver applicable to NAICS 325120, and is being broadened to the total small business pool to increase competition. Clarify equipment disposition and transition terms for the existing bulk oxygen system, as set forth in the revised Statement of Work below, so that all small business offerors can price the requirement on comparable terms. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.6, "Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services," as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as an RFQ. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2025-04. This solicitation is set-aside 100% for Total Small Business. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 325120, (Industrial Gas Manufacturing), with a size standard of 1,200 employees. This acquisition is subject to the SBA Nonmanufacturer Rule (NMR); a class waiver applicable to this NAICS code permits small business nonmanufacturers/resellers to furnish the product of a non-small manufacturer in accordance with 13 CFR 121.406(b) and FAR 52.219-33. The FSC/PSC is 6835. The White River Junction VAMC is seeking a qualified small business vendor capable of providing Medical-Grade Bulk Liquid Oxygen Deliveries for the VA White River Junction Healthcare System per the Performance Work Statement below. All interested small business companies shall provide quotations for the following: Supplies/Services ITEM NUMBER DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES QUANTITY UNIT UNIT PRICE AMOUNT 0001 Bulk Oxygen Supply Services in accordance with the SOW Period: Base 12.00 MO __________________ __________________ 0002 Tank Rental Services in accordance with the SOW Period: Base 1.00 EA __________________ __________________ 1001 Bulk Oxygen Supply Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY 1 12.00 MO __________________ __________________ 1002 Tank Rental Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY 1 1.00 YR __________________ __________________ 2001 Bulk Oxygen Supply Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY2 12.00 MO __________________ __________________ 2002 Tank Rental Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY 2 1.00 YR __________________ __________________ 3001 Bulk Oxygen Supply Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY 3 12.00 MO __________________ __________________ 3002 Tank Rental Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY 3 1.00 YR __________________ __________________ 4001 Bulk Oxygen Supply Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY 4 12.00 MO __________________ __________________ 4002 Tank Rental Services in accordance with the SOW Period: OY 4 1.00 YR __________________ __________________ TOTAL __________________ __________________ STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) VA White River Junction Healthcare System MEDICAL-GRADE LIQUID BULK OXYGEN 1. General The purpose of this requirement is to establish a committed source of supply of medical-grade bulk liquid oxygen for the VA White River Junction Healthcare System located in White River Junction, VT. The contractor shall also provide the necessary maintenance and monitoring of the complete bulk liquid oxygen distribution system, including the primary and reserve bulk tanks and reserve bottle bank, local alarm panel, and telemetry monitoring system, in accordance with the Equipment Disposition and Transition provisions of Section 2 below. The facility's annual requirements are estimated at 6,055,000 Standard Cubic Feet (SCF). There is no express or implied guarantee that these quantities will be purchased. The base contract period for all contracts awarded under this solicitation will be from date of award through a one year period with four continuing option years to equal the term of five years. Equipment rental shall be fixed not to exceed for the entire term. Pricing for all preventative maintenance, on-call 24/7 service must be included with the equipment rental pricing. A Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) has been designated in the solicitation schedule for the facility. The COR is responsible for local contract administration issues such as ordering and providing specific delivery instructions. A letter of delegation that outlines the COR's specific responsibilities will be provided to the contractor and COR at the time of contract award by the Contracting Officer. Within 15 days after notification of contract award, the contractor shall meet with the COR to ensure mutual understanding of facility requirements relating to the ordering method and specific details of any delivery instructions that are included in the solicitation schedule. Prior to first filling, contractor must perform in-service training to include the following facets for contractor owned and government owned systems: the refill procedure, an explanation and certification of all the liquid level low, volume alarm and high and low pressure set-points. The contractor will provide written procedures and training for VA staff for protocols to accomplish emergency shutdowns or other sudden, unplanned termination of the refilling process. Contractor will provide 24/7 emergency contact name(s) and telephone number(s). Prior to first filling, and annually thereafter, alarm set-point testing and written verification must be presented by the Contractor through the use of a qualified third party expert per NFPA 99, current Edition for contractor owned systems. Prior to first filling, and annually thereafter, the contractor must verify, in writing, the accuracy of all gauges and telemetry devices on contractor owned tanks. 2. Equipment Disposition and Transition This section is added by Amendment 0004 to clarify equipment terms and allow all small business offerors, including non-incumbent offerors, to price this requirement on comparable terms. The primary bulk oxygen tank (3,000-gallon), reserve tank (500-gallon), and associated alarm, telemetry, and ancillary equipment currently installed at the facility are owned by the incumbent contractor. Offerors shall price their quotation using one of the following two approaches, and shall clearly identify which approach is reflected in their price schedule: Option A � Use of Existing Equipment. The offeror proposes to negotiate use of the existing contractor-owned equipment (through purchase, lease, or subcontract arrangement with the incumbent or equipment owner) and to continue operating the current bulk tank and reserve system in place, subject to the offeror's own inspection, verification, and assumption of liability for the equipment during the period of performance. title: B--Intent to Award Notice: University of Minnesota
description: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Florence Bascom Geoscience Center, intends to award a non-competitive purchase order to Regents of the University of Minnesota, University of Minnesota (U of M), located in Duluth, MN, for a suite of geochemical analyses on water and sediment samples in direct support of the research project, Drought and Flood Extremes of the Continental United States: Past to Present., to be delivered to Reston, VA for the period of 9/21/2026 to 9/20/2027 with four (4) Option Years as follows: Option Year One (1): 09/21/2027 - 09/20/2028 Option Year Two (2): 09/21/2028 - 09/20/2029 Option Year Three (3): 09/21/2029 - 09/20/2030 Option Year Four (4): 09/21/2030 - 09/20/2031 The study conducted in this research project necessitates freeze coring to preserve the structure of mm-scale, water saturated seasonally-deposited layers. The only way to ensure preservation of these layers is by flash freezing the sediments at the bottom of the lake and keeping the "freeze core" completely frozen during transport and analyses. The U of M offers the only nearby facility where the frozen cores can be stored and analyzed over the duration of the five-year research project, which allows for short transport in a cooler on dry ice from each of the six to twelve study sites, where each core is collected. Transport between the study sites or frozen storage must be within a 200-mile radius and a few hours' drive in order to keep the samples firmly frozen during transport. The U of M is the only facility within the required radius offering stable isotope, elemental abundance, mineralogy, or major ion measurements of environmental samples. Analyzing a frozen core at the micron scale on an x-ray fluorescence scanner takes 6-8 hours, which would ordinarily result in melting. UMD has previously co-developed a distinctive method for scanning a frozen core. As a result, UMD and the technical staff are uniquely capable of carrying out these analyses without destruction of the freeze cores, as required. The University of Minnesota also provides in-kind support in the forms of unique specialized expertise of stable isotopic processes, student and technician time, and facility and equipment access. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 5.101(c)(4)(vi), all responsible sources may submit a quotation which shall be considered by the agency, however, THIS NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTATIONS. The Government intends to award this requirement noncompetitively in accordance with RFO 12.102(a). Responses must be emailed to Contracting Officer, Leah Williams, at leah_williams@ios.doi.gov. Reference Solicitation # DOIGFBO260040 in the subject line. The NAICS code is 541380. The size standard is $19 million. The anticipated award date is 09/18/2026. The anticipated contract will be firm fixed-price. A vendor must be registered at https://www.sam.gov to be awarded the purchase order.

title: Italy – Stationery – FORNITURA DI CANCELLERIA E CARTA MEDIANTE CATALOGO ELETTRONICO, COMPRENSIVA DI TRASPORTO (CONSEGNA) E RELATIVI SERVIZI ACCESSORI
description: Accordo Quadro con un unico operatore ai sensi dell’art. 59 comma 3 del Codice avente ad oggetto la fornitura, mediante catalogo elettronico, di cancelleria e carta comprensiva di trasporto (consegna) e relativi servizi accessori per Rai S.p.A. e relative consociate, quali Rai Com S.p.A. Rai Cinema S.p.A. e Rai Pubblicità S.p.A.. Per consentire il confronto competitivo è stato individuato un paniere di prodotti in funzione dei consumi storici e rappresentativo delle principali categorie di acquisto della Stazione appaltante, articolato nelle due categorie merceologiche della cancelleria e della carta per fotocopie e stampa. È altresì previsto l’approvvigionamento di articoli non ricompresi nel paniere, ma appartenenti alle medesime categorie merceologiche oggetto dell’affidamento ed, a tal fine, l’aggiudicatario dovrà rendere disponibile il proprio catalogo elettronico di prodotti che, allegato all’Accordo Quadro, costituirà il riferimento contrattuale per l’acquisizione dei prodotti non inclusi nel paniere e potrà essere aggiornato nel corso dell'esecuzione mediante inserimento di nuovi articoli o sostituzione di prodotti non più commercializzati. Tale impostazione consente di effettuare il confronto concorrenziale sulla componente maggiormente rappresentativa dei consumi aziendali, garantendo al contempo la necessaria flessibilità per l’acquisizione di ulteriori articoli appartenenti alle medesime categorie merceologiche, non preventivamente stimabili in termini quantitativi, mantenendo condizioni economiche coerenti con quelle risultanti dalla procedura di gara. Il Capitolato Tecnico, cui si rinvia, prevede altresì i seguenti servizi accessori: - messa a disposizione di una piattaforma e-procurement in grado di gestire un numero illimitato di profili di navigazione e che consenta le funzionalità di cui al Capitolato tecnico, tra cui, a mero titolo esemplificativo, la consultazione di un catalogo elettronico e l’estrazione di report sintetici di dettaglio; - attivazione di un servizio di call center dalle ore 09.00 alle ore 17:00 di tutti i giorni lavorativi; - reportistica trimestrale di dati aggregati per singola categoria merceologica; - imballaggio, trasporto e recapito al piano (cd. punto di consegna) presso le sedi indicate nel Capitolato Tecnico e dislocate sull’intero territorio nazionale. In particolare, è richiesto che la fornitura sia gestita mediante ordinativi su catalogo elettronico globale dedicato, con caratteristiche e funzionalità (consultazione, ricerca articolo, invio ordine ecc.) corrispondenti a quanto descritto nel Capitolato Tecnico e relative appendici. Pertanto, condizione necessaria per il corretto espletamento della fornitura è che ciascun concorrente offra la possibilità di disporre di un proprio "portale internet” ove vengano riportati, resi visibili e disponibili per l’acquisto mediante "carrello elettronico" i prodotti oggetto del proprio listino di vendita, come descritto nel Capitolato tecnico. La fornitura è infine comprensiva di ogni onere relativo a trasporto, imballaggio e protezione fino alla consegna. La fornitura è comprensiva delle schede tecniche e di sicurezza dei materiali forniti e delle dichiarazioni di conformità rilasciate dal produttore a norma di legge. Per la dettagliata descrizione delle caratteristiche tecniche e funzionali della fornitura nonché delle modalità di esecuzione della stessa si rimanda alla documentazione tecnica allegata alle citate RdA. Con riferimento alla fornitura di carta, assumono rilievo i Criteri Ambientali minimi per la fornitura di carta in risme (c.d. CAM) di cui al Decreto del Ministero dell’ambiente e della tutela del territorio e del mare del 4 aprile 2013.

title: Italy – General management consultancy services – Servizi di consulenza strategica in favore di RAI S.p.A.
description: l servizio è articolato nei seguenti ambiti principali, con riferimento ai quali l’aggiudicatario sarà chiamato a svolgere le attività descritte nel Capitolato Tecnico per il soddisfacimento dei diversi fabbisogni: a) servizi di consulenza per lo sviluppo di piani industriali, comprensivi delle relative analisi strategiche ed economico-finanziarie; b) servizi di consulenza strategica per singoli progetti aziendali, incluse iniziative di sviluppo industriale, razionalizzazione organizzativa, sviluppo tecnologico, valutazione di sinergie industriali e operazioni di riassetto societario o di Gruppo; c) servizi di program/project management a supporto dell’implementazione di piani industriali e di progetti strategici comprensivi delle attività di monitoraggio, gestione del cambiamento organizzativo, misurazione delle performance, reporting direzionale e supporto al conseguimento degli obiettivi progettuali. Le attività potranno comportare la predisposizione di studi, analisi, business plan, proiezioni economico-finanziarie, documenti programmatici, piani di lavoro, report direzionali, cruscotti di monitoraggio e ogni altra documentazione funzionale al perseguimento degli obiettivi definiti da RAI. L’aggiudicatario dovrà supportare RAI in relazione ai fabbisogni di volta in volta espressi nell’ambito dei servizi oggetto dell'Accordo Quadro, garantendo per tutta la durata contrattuale la disponibilità di professionalità idonee a presidiare l'intera gamma delle attività previste dalla documentazione di gara nonché la capacità organizzativa necessaria ad assicurare, ove richiesto, la contemporanea esecuzione di più interventi progettuali. La regolamentazione progettuale ed economica delle prestazioni è basata sul modello settimane/Full Time Equivalent (FTE). Il corrispettivo di ciascun intervento sarà determinato sulla base dell'effort progettuale stimato e della composizione del team richiesta, definita mediante il mix delle figure professionali previste dal Capitolato Tecnico e calibrata in funzione della complessità, della durata, degli obiettivi e degli output dell'incarico. Le attività saranno attivate mediante specifici contratti attuativi, nell’ambito dei quali saranno individuati il dimensionamento dell’intervento, il team di riferimento e le relative modalità di esecuzione. Le risorse impiegate nell’esecuzione dei servizi resteranno in ogni momento alle esclusive dipendenze dell’aggiudicatario e opereranno sotto la sua direzione, coordinamento e responsabilità organizzativa. L’aggiudicatario conserverà in via esclusiva ogni potere datoriale, gerarchico, organizzativo, disciplinare e gestionale nei confronti delle risorse impiegate. RAI definirà esclusivamente il fabbisogno, gli obiettivi dell’intervento, gli output attesi, le relative tempistiche, le modalità di interazione con le proprie strutture, le eventuali sedi di svolgimento delle attività e i criteri di verifica delle prestazioni rese. Resteranno di esclusiva competenza dell’aggiudicatario l’organizzazione operativa delle attività, l’individuazione delle risorse da impiegare e la gestione del team di progetto, fermo restando il rispetto dei requisiti professionali previsti dalla documentazione di gara e di quanto eventualmente offerto in sede di gara. Per la dettagliata descrizione delle caratteristiche tecniche e funzionali del servizio nonché delle modalità di esecuzione dello stesso si rimanda alla documentazione tecnica di gara. Ai sensi dell’art. 120 comma 1 lettera a) del Codice, Rai S.p.A. si riserva: - la facoltà, qualora l’importo contrattuale non dovesse essere esaurito alla scadenza del termine di durata contrattuale di estendere la durata del relativo contratto per il tempo necessario all’utilizzo dell’intero importo contrattuale; - la facoltà di richiedere all’appaltatore, nel corso della durata del contratto, in caso di esigenze sopravvenute che determino un incremento o decremento del fabbisogno di servizi, un aumento o diminuzione delle prestazioni, a parità di condizioni, per un importo fino ad euro 360.000,00, anche ai sensi dell’art. 120 comma 9 del Codice; in tal evenienza l'appaltatore non può fare valere il diritto alla risoluzione del contratto. In casi eccezionali, al verificarsi delle condizioni indicate all’art. 120 comma 11 del Codice, la durata del contratto (se del caso come estesa ai sensi dell’art. 120, comma 1, lett. a) del Codice come sopra previsto), ancora in corso di esecuzione, potrà essere prorogata per il tempo strettamente necessario alla conclusione della procedura di individuazione del nuovo contraente. In tal caso l’appaltatore sarà tenuto all’esecuzione delle prestazioni oggetto del contratto agli stessi prezzi, patti e condizioni previsti nello stesso.

description: D 162 - Spotřební a nespotřební zdravotnický materiál Požadujeme dodat materiál, který bude zdravotnickým prostředkem splňujícím specifikaci v příloze k tomuto zadání. Nabízený zdravotnický materiál musí splňovat VEŠKERÉ PARAMETRY A ZADANÉ POŽADAVKY. Zdravotnické prostředky dle zákona č. 375/2022 Sb. dodat vč. EU prohlášení o shodě podle zákona č. 90/2016 Sb. o posuzování shody stanovených výrobků při jejich dodávání na trh (CE štítek, Declaration of Conformity) v listinné či elektronické podobě. Součástí dodávky musí být návod k použití ke každé položce (je-li výrobcem vydán) v českém jazyce. Uchazeč k nabídce vloží i obrázek a technický popis nabízeného materiálu, který by byl v případě vítězství v soutěži dodán pro porovnání splnění všech zadaných parametrů. Spotřební materiál musí mít exspiraci minimálně 18 měsíců dobu použitelnosti od data dodání kupujícímu. V případě, že výrobce uvádí dobu použitelnosti kratší, pak je nutno dodat materiál, jehož doba použitelnosti bude minimálně 2/3 ve prospěch kupujícího od data předání kupujícímu. V případě, že z doložitelných důvodů není možné stanovené doby použitelnosti dodržet, je nutno před započetím dodávky toto konzultovat s kupujícím.

title: Germany – Canteen services – Bewirtschaftung der Kantine
description: Die Qualitäts- und Unterstützungsagentur - Landesinstitut für Schule des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (QUA-LiS NRW) will den Betrieb der Kantine neu vergeben. Die QUA-LiS NRW unterhält einen Tagungsbetrieb mit 28 Tagungsräumen für 5 bis ca. 200 Personen nebst 115 Gästezimmern. Im Regelfall werden ein- bis dreitägige Veranstaltungen durchgeführt. Während der Schulferien in Nordrhein-Westfalen und an den Wochenenden ruht der Tagungsbetrieb üblicherweise bzw. ist erheblich reduziert, so dass nur die Mitarbeitenden der QUA-LiS NRW die Kantine nutzen. Die QUA-LiS NRW beabsichtigt, die Bewirtschaftung der Kantine (einschließlich Küche und Nebenräumen) in ihren Räumlichkeiten in Soest zum 1. Februar 2027 neu zu vergeben. Die Vergabe des Betriebs der Kantine erfolgt im Rahmen eines Dienstleistungsvertrages gemäß § 103 GWB. Hierbei stellt die Auftraggeberin der/dem Auftragnehmenden die zur Erbringung der Leistung erforderliche Infrastruktur zur Verfügung. Das wirtschaftliche Risiko der Betriebsführung trägt die/der Aufragnehmende. Der Dienstleistungsvertrag ist auf 4 Jahre und 6 Monate befristet sein. Er soll am 01.02.2027 beginnen und am 31.07.2031 enden. Für den Auftraggeber besteht die Option das Vertragsverhältnis einmalig um ein Jahr bis längstens zum 31.07.2032 zu verlängern.

description: Das Schillerplatzareal in Iserlohn befindet sich im Zentrum der Stadt und stellt eine der wichtigsten Entwicklungsflächen im Rahmen der städtischen Erneuerungsstrategie dar. Ziel ist es, die städtebauliche Qualität und die Nutzungsvielfalt im Innenstadtbereich nachhaltig zu verbessern und die Funktion des Schillerplatzes als urbanes Zentrum zu stärken. Das Areal umfasst rd. 12.000 m² und liegt in direkter Nachbarschaft zu Rathaus, Stadt-Sparkasse, Stadthotel und Fußgängerzone, welche zugleich die südliche Grenze des Areals bildet. Dadurch ist eine direkte Anbindung an die wichtigsten innerstädtischen Verkehrs- und Aufenthaltsbereiche gewährleistet. Im Vorfeld der geplanten Entwicklung wurden bereits wesentliche vorbereitende Maßnahmen auf der Projektfläche durchgeführt, darunter der Abriss der ehemaligen Karstadt-Immobilie und der zugehörigen Tiefgarage sowie die Erkundung und Sicherung unterirdischer Hohlräume (Verkarstung und Erz-Bergbau). Unmittelbar an das Projektareal angrenzend (nördliche Seite des Theodor-Heuss-Rings) befindet sich derzeit das Rathaus I. Mit dem Abbruch des Rathaus I. wird voraussichtlich noch in 2026 begonnen. Zielvorgaben, Umfang und terminliche Umsetzung für einen möglichen Neubau an diesem Ort sind noch nicht bekannt. Das Schillerplatzareal und sein Umfeld bieten somit die Voraussetzungen für eine umfassende städtebauliche Entwicklung und das Projektareal stellt einen zentralen Baustein für die zukünftige Gestaltung und Nutzung der Iserlohner Innenstadt dar.

title: Germany – Resurfacing works – Landesstraßen im Landkreis Nordhausen; Beseitigung Fahrbahnschäden, Abschnittsweise Deckenerneuerung - Rahmenvereinbarung 2026/2027
description: Es handelt sich um eine Rahmenvereinbarung gemäß § 4a EU VOB/A. Das bedeutet, dass die Bedingungen für Einzelaufträge innerhalb der Laufzeit der Rahmenvereinbarung festgelegt werden sollen. Dies betrifft insbesondere die in Aussicht genommenen Preise. Die Rahmenvereinbarung wird mit einem Unternehmen geschlossen. Das in Aussicht genommene Auftragsvolumen wurde so genau wie möglich ermittelt, wird aber nicht abschließend festgelegt. Es besteht kein Anspruch auf eine komplette Leistungsausführung lt. Leistungsverzeichnis. Der Leistungsumfang kann sich bei einzelnen Positionen erheblich erhöhen, aber auch ganz entfallen. Es ist vorgesehen innerhalb der Grundlaufzeit (09.11.2026 – 31.12.2027) bis zu fünf Einzelmaßnahmen in Form räumlich abgegrenzter, zusammenhängender Streckenabschnitte auszuführen. Für die Kalkulation kann von mindestens 3 Einzelaufträgen ausgegangen werden. Diese sind bereits konkret bekannt und betreffen folgende Streckenabschnitte: L 3080 Nordhausen - Bielen vNK 4530 014 nNK 4531 049Y L 3080 Bielen - AS Heringen vNK 4530 014 nNK 4531 049Y L 3080 AS Heringen - Urbach VnK 4531 049X nNK 4531 012 Die im Leistungsverzeichnis angegebenen Mengen beruhen auf Erfahrungswerten vergleichbarer Maßnahmen und stellen unverbindliche Schätzmengen dar. Sie dienen ausschließlich der Kalkulation der Angebote. Bei einer Vertragsverlängerung (gem. Punkt 5.1.1 Optionen) kann davon ausgegangen werden, dass mindestens 1 und maximal 3 Einzelmaßnahmen je Verlängerungsjahr beauftragt werden. Die Sanierung erfolgt im Wesentlichen durch die Herstellung neuer bituminöser Fahrbahnaufbauten. Abhängig vom jeweiligen Schadensbild reicht der Sanierungsumfang von der Erneuerung einzelner Asphaltschichten bis zur vollständigen Erneuerung des Oberbaus einschließlich Trag-, Binder- und Deckschicht. Die erforderlichen Aufbruch- bzw. Frästiefen können zwischen 4 cm und ca. 25 cm liegen und werden im Einzelfall durch den Auftraggeber festgelegt.

title: Secure Packaged Microelectronic Components, Printed Circuit Boards, and Supporting Technologies
description: Information Requested: The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Aviation and Missile Center (DEVCOM AvMC), Redstone Arsenal, AL is conducting market research to identify domestic products, suppliers, designers and manufacturers of advanced protection architectures, systems, components, and other technologies for packaged microelectronics intended for deployment into current and future military systems of interest to the Department of Defense (DoD). This RFI is seeking information from suitable vendors/vendor teams related to the following Technology Areas: 1. Board-level Security: Capabilities spanning microelectronic components and portable soft IP integrated with commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) devices across modular open systems architectures (MOSA) form factor systems (e.g., 3U/6U OpenVPX/SOSA, 3U/6U SpaceVPX, VNX, and smaller). 2. Package Security: Specialized microelectronics packaging configurations or designs for multi-chip modules (MCMs) or systems-in-package (SIPs) which utilize COTS or bespoke security components that are intended to provide additional security to underlying components. 3. Enhanced Secure Boot: Portable soft IP that can be used in conjunction with COTS microelectronic components to provide additional security for enhanced secure boot applications. 4. Secure Components: Purpose-designed microelectronic components (chiplets, ASICs, etc.) that are intended to provide enhanced trust/security for co-packaged microelectronic components. 5. Multi-chip Packaging: Advanced microelectronics packaging techniques that inherently provide additional component security or could be easily adapted to provide additional microelectronic component security. 6. Emerging Technologies: Novel techniques, materials, and processes that are compatible with modern microelectronic manufacturing/packaging methods that can provide additional security to packaged microelectronic components. 7. Other: Technologies, methods, and processes not mentioned above that are compatible with modern microelectronics design, manufacturing, and packaging techniques and able to provide enhanced security to packaged microelectronic components. For additional details refer to the Attachment, R2.0_SS_RFI_SUBMISSION_v1.2.

title: ISBEE Set-Aside: Exercise Equipment for the Great Plains Area IHS Youth Regional Treatment Center
description: **AMENDMENT ONE (1) ADDS QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS TO THE SOLICITATION. THE SUBMISSION DEADLINE IS NOT CHANGED.** Combined Synopsis � Solicitation 75H70626Q00233 The Aberdeen Area Indian Health Service (IHS) is soliciting quotations for the purchase of commercial-grade fitness equipment, including delivery, assembly, installation, operational verification, orientation, and warranty documentation, for the Great Plains Area Youth Regional Treatment Center (YRTC), 12451 SD-1806, Mobridge, South Dakota 57601. The acquisition is issued as RFQ 75H70626Q00233 and is a 100% Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE) set-aside under the Buy Indian Act. The applicable NAICS code is 423910. Requirement The contractor will furnish and install six pieces of commercial fitness equipment, or technically acceptable equal products: | 1 | Inflight Fitness Multi Bicep/Tricep, 150-lb stack, CT-MBTS-150 | 2 | Inflight Fitness Multi Inner/Outer Thigh, 150-lb stack, CT-MIOS-150 | 3 | Inflight Fitness Multi Seated Leg Extension/Leg Curl, 250-lb stack, CT-MSECS-250 | 4 | Inflight Fitness Multi Press, 250-lb stack, CT-MPSS-250 | 5 | Inflight Fitness Multi Leg Press, 250-lb stack, CT-MLPS-250 | 6 | Muscle D Commercial Stair Climber with LED Console, CC-SC-LS-B Shipping is identified separately as Item 7. The identified brands/models establish the type of equipment contemplated rather than an absolute brand restriction. Equal products may be offered if they satisfy the solicitation's salient functional and performance characteristics. Reference-product dimensions and weights are principally for delivery and installation planning and are not exact design restrictions unless necessary to fit the Government-designated installation area. Quantities are firm requirements. Delivery and Performance Performance begins upon award. The contractor must complete delivery, installation, operational verification, orientation, and submission of warranty documentation within 30�60 calendar days after award, unless the award establishes another completion date or the Contracting Officer subsequently changes it in writing. Contractors are required to promptly advise the Contracting Officer of anticipated commercial supply-chain delays. Pricing is to be FOB Destination and must include packaging, handling, shipping, and delivery. Unit prices are described as all-inclusive of costs associated with performance. Competition and Eligibility Competition is limited to concerns that qualify as both an Indian Economic Enterprise and a small business concern. Firms that do not meet both requirements will not be considered. Offerors must submit the required Indian Economic Enterprise Representation Form and represent that they meet the IEE definition and will continue to meet it throughout contract performance. Offerors must also have an active SAM.gov registration and current UEI before award and certify that they are an authorized reseller of the products proposed and that applicable manufacturer warranties will be fully honored. Evaluation and Award The procurement uses a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) approach. Award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price whose quotation is technically acceptable and whose past performance is acceptable, if evaluated. The Government intends to evaluate quotations without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussions. Technical evaluation is Acceptable/Unacceptable. To receive an Acceptable rating, the quotation must demonstrate compliance with all material solicitation requirements, including specifications, salient characteristics, delivery requirements, and mandatory technical requirements. An Unacceptable quotation is ineligible for award. Price will be evaluated for total evaluated price and may also be assessed for reasonableness and completeness. Past performance may be rated Acceptable, Unacceptable, or Neutral. CPARS will be the primary source; when CPARS information is unavailable, an offeror may use the solicitation's Past Performance Questionnaire. Offerors may provide up to three references for recent and relevant contracts/orders performed within the preceding five years involving work similar in scope, size, and complexity. A firm without relevant past performance is not evaluated favorably or unfavorably. Submission Requirements and Key Dates The solicitation was issued September 2, 2026. Questions must be emailed to the Contract Specialist by 4:00 p.m. CDT on September 9, 2026. Written quotations are due 5:00 p.m. CDT on September 16, 2026. Email submissions are permitted; facsimile submissions are not, and no original hard copy is required. The solicitation identifies three attachments that form part of the procurement package: 1. SOW_YRTC_Fitness_Equipment 2. Indian Firm Representation Form-26Q00233 3. Past Performance Questionnaire Contract Administration Invoices must be submitted electronically through the Department of Treasury's Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) in accordance with HHSAR 352.232-71, unless the Contracting Officer authorizes an alternate method in writing. Required invoice information includes the contractor name, invoice number/date, complete award number, description/quantity/pricing, shipping and payment terms, UEI/TIN, and contractor contact information. In summary: this is a Buy Indian, 100% ISBEE-set-aside commercial-item procurement for six installed pieces of fitness equipment at the Mobridge YRTC. The Government is seeking a compliant, technically acceptable solution�including delivery and installation�at the lowest evaluated price, with contractor eligibility, technical compliance, delivery capability, authorized-reseller/warranty status, and past performance forming the principal award considerations.

description: Sources Sought Notice U.S. Embassy Mexico�International Narcotics & Law Enforcement Affairs (INL Mexico) Equipment for Mexican Vetted Units INL Mexico seeks to provide tactical, ballistics, and personal protective equipment (PPE) to INL-supported vetted units, as well as federal and state task forces that collaborate with U.S. law enforcement agencies to disrupt cartel-related illicit activities. These units play a critical role in seizing fentanyl and other illicit drugs and goods, apprehending fugitives and individuals affiliated with cartels, and investigating cases linked to transnational criminal organizations (TCOs). This Sources Sought Notice is part of the U.S. Government's market research efforts to identify capable small business vendors that are qualified and capable to deliver equipment for the U.S. Embassy Mexico City that will be donated to vetted units of Mexican agencies. The information gathered will help inform future procurement strategies and requirements including selection of applicable socioeconomic programs and small business set-asides for future procurement. This Sources Sought is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this notice. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, IFB, or RFP, if any is issued. This equipment donation consists of twenty-seven individual types of equipment organized into three groups: Group 1: Personal Protective Equipment 6 Equpiment Line Items Planned NAICS Code: 423990 Group 2: Tactical Equipment 16 Equipment Line Items Planned NAICS Code: 423850 Group 3: Ballistics Equipment 5 Equipment Line Items Planned NAICS Code: 315990 All equipment must be provided through manufacturer approved distribution channels and must be new. The government contemplates issuance of an RFQ that permits firms to quote on one, two, or all three equipment groups. However, quoting firms must be able to provide all equipment types within each group. The contractor must be able to deliver the equipment to a receiving location in Brownsville, Texas, and provide personnel to participate in a joint inspection and inventory with personnel from the Department of State. It is anticipated that the SOW will require that the contractor provide in country warranty support of required items Notice Responses/capability statements should respond to the Draft Statement of Work and be formatted in accordance with the Sources Sought Instructions file. Do not include the following in the response: Do not submit formal proposals or offers; Do not submit requests to be considered for award or to be notified of a future solicitation; as a courtesy to vendors who submit capability statements, responding vendors will be notified should the government elect to issue a formal RFP/RFQ at a later date. Do not submit requests to be added to a mailing or distribution list; Do not submit questions or comments not related to this Request for Information; Do not respond via telephone. How to Submit Responses: Please submit responses via email to ModrakER@state.gov including �19AQMM26N0004: �Vetted Unit Equipment� in the e-mail subject line. In addition to a completed Equipment Specs Excel type file, please submit capability statement responses as a single attachment to the email: either Adobe pdf file or MS Word file. If you have any questions regarding this Notice, please submit them via e-mail to ModrakER@state.gov. Please include 19AQMM26N0004 in the e-mail subject line. The Request for Information submission closing date is September 16 2026, at 4:00 PM CST.
